evidence.claim: The President serves a five-year term with only one reelection, is supreme commander of the armed forces, and may declare war, make peace, and conclude treaties with DPR approval.
evidence.title: Indonesia 1945 (reinst. 1959, rev. 2002) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: The President serves a five-year term with only one reelection, is supreme commander of the armed forces, and may declare war, make peace, and conclude treaties with DPR approval.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Constitutional text directly fixes the term ceiling and the treaty/war powers relevant to existential-risk exposure.
evidence.period_fit: Defines the 2022 ceiling and the absence of open-ended tenure or nuclear command authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct institutional authority; Jokowi had war/treaty powers only within constitutional approval rules.
contrary_evidence: Indonesia is not a nuclear-armed state, so these powers do not translate into nuclear-use authority.

evidence.claim: Indonesia deposited its CTBT ratification instrument at the UN in 2012 and became the 157th state to ratify the treaty.
evidence.title: Indonesia Deposits Instrument of Ratification to the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia deposited its CTBT ratification instrument at the UN in 2012 and became the 157th state to ratify the treaty.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN disarmament office notice gives the date, act, and treaty significance directly.
evidence.period_fit: Baseline treaty posture in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level treaty commitment predating Jokowi; relevant as inherited posture.
contrary_evidence: CTBT is not in force globally, so ratification is normative but not a complete arms-control endpoint.

evidence.claim: The Bangkok Treaty obliges parties not to develop, manufacture, acquire, possess, station, transport, test, or use nuclear weapons, and to use nuclear material and facilities exclusively for peaceful purposes.
evidence.title: Treaty on the Southeast Asia Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone (Bangkok Treaty)
evidence.publisher: United Nations Platform for Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zones
evidence.excerpt: The Bangkok Treaty obliges parties not to develop, manufacture, acquire, possess, station, transport, test, or use nuclear weapons, and to use nuclear material and facilities exclusively for peaceful purposes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN nuclear-weapon-free-zone page summarizes the treaty's core obligations and membership.
evidence.period_fit: Directly shapes Indonesia's nuclear posture in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level obligation; Jokowi inherited and administered within this legal framework.
contrary_evidence: The treaty does not eliminate all regional nuclear risk because external nuclear-weapon-state assurances remained incomplete.

evidence.claim: In 2022 ASEAN leaders reaffirmed preserving Southeast Asia as a zone free of nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction, and the Plan of Action to Strengthen the Implementation of the Bangkok Treaty was renewed for 2023-2027.
evidence.title: UNODA 2022 Yearbook, Chapter 4
evidence.publisher: United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 ASEAN leaders reaffirmed preserving Southeast Asia as a zone free of nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction, and the Plan of Action to Strengthen the Implementation of the Bangkok Treaty was renewed for 2023-2027.
evidence.source_locator: Treaty on the Southeast Asia Nuclear Weapon-Free Zone section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN yearbook provides contemporaneous regional summary, though it is not a direct Jokowi statement.
evidence.period_fit: Matches the 2022 regional environment in which Indonesia operated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Regional/ASEAN posture rather than personal Jokowi conduct; still relevant to the inherited baseline.
contrary_evidence: The same source notes that none of the five nuclear-weapon states had signed the Bangkok Treaty protocol by end-2022.

evidence.claim: BAPETEN received a consultation request from PT ThorCon Power Indonesia for an NPP, and the consultation framework included a roadmap for NPP design development and safety to be implemented in 2023.
evidence.title: BAPETEN Receives Consultation Request for Nuclear Power Plant Development
evidence.excerpt: BAPETEN received a consultation request from PT ThorCon Power Indonesia for an NPP, and the consultation framework included a roadmap for NPP design development and safety to be implemented in 2023.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct regulator notice with date, parties, and technical scope for the consultation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-regulatory context under Jokowi; the source does not show a personal presidential decision, only a state process.
contrary_evidence: It shows exploratory civilian nuclear planning, not weapons policy or catastrophic escalation.

evidence.claim: The energy minister said the government was considering Russia's offer to develop an NPP, while the national roadmap projected nuclear energy need only starting around 2040.
evidence.title: Govt mulling Russia's offer to develop nuclear energy in Indonesia
evidence.excerpt: The energy minister said the government was considering Russia's offer to develop an NPP, while the national roadmap projected nuclear energy need only starting around 2040.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reporting is direct and dated, but the claim is ministerial and roadmap-based rather than a presidential act.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 policy discussion on civilian nuclear power.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level consideration under Jokowi; not a direct personal nuclear-risk choice by the president.
contrary_evidence: The article presents nuclear as a long-range energy option, not an urgent security necessity.

evidence.claim: Indonesia, speaking on behalf of NAM, reaffirmed the need for multilateral nuclear disarmament, supported CTBT, and emphasized that nuclear-weapon-free zones strengthen nonproliferation.
evidence.title: Dangers Posed by Nuclear Weapons Back in Global Spotlight, United Nations High Representative for Disarmament Affairs Tells First Committee
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia, speaking on behalf of NAM, reaffirmed the need for multilateral nuclear disarmament, supported CTBT, and emphasized that nuclear-weapon-free zones strengthen nonproliferation.
evidence.source_locator: Indonesia (on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement) statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting record captures a dated official statement from the Indonesian delegation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to Indonesia's delegation, not a direct Jokowi statement; still useful as state posture context.
contrary_evidence: This is diplomatic posture, not evidence of a ruler-level command or crisis choice in 2022.

evidence.claim: Indonesia told the First Committee that nuclear-weapon states should comply with their obligations, eliminate arsenals transparently, and that nuclear safety and security norms should be pursued within the IAEA framework.
evidence.title: Non-Nuclear-Armed States Get Nothing in Return for Fulfilling Commitments Except Threat of Potential Annihilation, First Committee Told
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia told the First Committee that nuclear-weapon states should comply with their obligations, eliminate arsenals transparently, and that nuclear safety and security norms should be pursued within the IAEA framework.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting record preserves the statement and its policy content directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level foreign-policy line rather than direct presidential choice.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is a multilateral statement, not evidence of Jokowi personally managing a nuclear crisis.
